# Truncating lower-dimensional endpoint contacts removes their stresses

This is an unrestricted extremal mechanism. Corner truncation increases
facet complexity; the argument is not valid inside a fixed triangle or
fixed-facet class unless that class explicitly permits the added truncations.

## 1. Quantitative polytope truncation lemma

Let K be a full-dimensional d-polytope, d>=2. A nonzero vector n exposes a
face F={x in K:n.x=h_K(n)} of dimension k<=d-2. Put

    K(t)=K intersect {x:n.x<=h_K(n)-t},      t>=0 small.

Then

    |K minus K(t)|=O(t^(d-k))=o(t),                                (1)
    h_K(t)(n)=h_K(n)-t.                                          (2)

Every halfspace cap changes by at most the removed volume, uniformly over
all ambient halfspaces if this is one integer fiber. In particular both its
volume and every cap mass have zero first derivative in t.

For (1), triangulate K into finitely many full-dimensional simplices using
its vertices. In a simplex meeting F, its vertices on F form a face of
dimension f<=k. In barycentric coordinates the normal deficit is
sum_(off-F vertices) delta_i lambda_i, with each delta_i>0. Truncation requires
all d-f off-face coordinates to be O(t); integrating the remaining bounded
coordinates gives O(t^(d-f)), hence O(t^(d-k)). Simplices not meeting F have
a positive normal gap and contribute nothing for small t. Formula (2)
follows by intersecting the cut plane with an edge leaving F.

A further estimate is needed when the body's and target facet's affine
parameters move. There are constants C,t0,epsilon>0 such that for
|m-n|<epsilon and 0<=t<t0,

    h_K(m)-h_K(t)(m)>=t(1-C|m-n|).                              (3)

Indeed, for m near n the maximizing old vertices lie in F. The new vertices
which can maximize m are intersections of the cut plane with edges from a
vertex v of F to a vertex outside F. They have the form v+t a_e, with
n.a_e=-1 and a_e in a fixed finite list. Hence
m.(v+t a_e)<=h_K(m)-t(1-C|m-n|). Old vertices outside F retain a fixed normal
gap and cannot maximize for small t. This proves (3).

Under a nearby affine map A x+c, the comparison normal in reference
coordinates is A^T m. Thus (3) gives a support improvement

    t+O(t |p|)

when all affine parameters p are small. The volume estimate (1) is uniform
under these affine maps.

## 2. Finite simultaneous truncations

For each endpoint e in {0,2} and each active middle-facet normal n_l which
exposes a face of dimension at most d-2 in Ke, introduce a parameter
sigma_e,l>=0 and truncate Ke by that normal at depth sigma_e,l in its
reference coordinates. There are finitely many parameters. Simultaneously
imposing all cuts can only decrease each endpoint support further. Its
volume loss is at most the sum of the individual removed volumes, therefore
is o(|sigma|), uniformly as sigma approaches0 in the nonnegative cone.
Every cap-mass difference is bounded by the same quantity.

Thus all objective and cap first derivatives in the sigma coordinates are
zero. This assertion is uniform in nearby affine/cap parameters; it is not
an interchange of a nonuniform cap limit with a derivative.

## 3. A sufficient first-order compatibility cone

Use the exact finite middle-facet/endpoint-vertex-pair compatibility model
from candidate 11e10da90bca54a3, allowing any polytopal
fibers and any finite number of middle facets. Before truncation, write its
smooth pair inequalities as g_l,ab(p)>=0. Let

    sigma_l=sum_(endpoints e cut in direction n_l) sigma_e,l.

The actual truncated support inequality is at least

    min_ab g_l,ab(p)+sigma_l+o(|p|+|sigma|).                       (4)

To verify (4), apply (3) to each endpoint cut in this indexed direction;
other cuts improve support and are discarded from this lower bound. The
error is O(|p| |sigma|), which is o(|p|+|sigma|). This remains valid at ties
between support vertices; the finite pair formulation retains all of them.

Consequently the finite polyhedral cone

    D g_l,ab(p)[delta p]+sigma_l>=0 for every active pair,
    sigma_e,l>=0,

together with the existing linear cap-cover constraints, is a SUFFICIENT
first-order feasibility cone. If these pair inequalities are strict, the
actual nonlinear constraints hold for all sufficiently small positive time
by (4). Nonactive pairs retain their strict gaps.

There is a simultaneous strictification direction. Choose q0 in int(K0),
q2 in int(K2), q1=(q0+q2)/2 in int(K1). Shrink all three bodies about qz by
the same factor. This is an ambient affine fiber map, so it preserves every
active midpoint equality and strictly decreases all active cap-gradient
choices. Add a tiny middle-only outward homothety about q1. Its derivative
on every active middle facet is strictly positive. It preserves the cap
strict decrease when the added coefficient is small. All sigma coordinates
are zero in this direction.

Therefore the same normalized finite-dimensional separation proof applies
to this sufficient cone. A hypothetical strict feasible improving direction
would integrate to an actual nearby compatible truncated family. Because the
minimum is unrestricted, all these competitors are authorized.

## 4. The endpoint contact multipliers vanish on nonfacets

Let eta_l,ab>=0 be the compatibility multipliers in the resulting normalized
stress, eta_l=sum_ab eta_l,ab, and zeta_e,l>=0 the multipliers for
sigma_e,l>=0. In the sigma_e,l coordinate the objective gradient and EVERY
cap-gradient choice are zero, while every pair constraint for facet l has
coefficient +1. The normalized stationarity equation is therefore

    0=-eta_l-zeta_e,l.

Both quantities are nonnegative, so

    eta_l=0 whenever n_l exposes a face of dimension<=d-2
            in EITHER endpoint fiber.                            (5)

Thus the normalized contact stress at an unrestricted positive polytopal
extremizer can be chosen to be supported only on middle-facet normals which
expose FACETS in BOTH endpoint fibers. Multiple support ties are retained,
and simultaneous cuts do not require a chosen triangulation or combinatorial
chamber to persist under the perturbation.

This does not say that the nonfacet contact equality disappears from the
body. It says it carries zero multiplier in a normalized stress obtained
using the enlarged admissible variation family.

## 5. Planar triangle consequence and remaining patterns

For three planar triangle fibers, every surviving stressed middle facet
must be parallel to an edge in EACH endpoint triangle. Hence:

* If the middle triangle has no facet direction shared by both endpoints,
  every eta vanishes. The strict-containment stress proof then applies
  algebraically, even though support contacts may exist: its middle normal
  balance and matrix equations are unforced, giving the midpoint-chord bound.
* If all three middle facet directions are shared by both endpoints and all
  three are tight, the triangles have a common normal fan and the centroid
  midpoint argument already proves the desired2/9 bound.
* The unresolved boundary patterns can therefore be restricted to one or two
  shared, stressed facet directions (or a proper subset of the common fan).

The first item yields a genuine local exclusion at an unrestricted attained
POLYTOPAL minimum, including rotated endpoint contact patterns whose contacts occur
only at vertices. It does not turn three tight support values into equality
of a triangle with a generally hexagonal Minkowski average.

At equality contacts the assertion that at most one endpoint is deepest
uses the midpoint-depth-plus-min lemma in candidate 2d61091414784568,
not strict Brunn--Minkowski containment: if both endpoint unnormalized depths
equal D>0, their centers' actual middle midpoint has mixed depth at least2D.
An unrestricted attained minimum is not known to be polytopal. Conversely,
the guaranteed polytopal minimum in a fixed shared-plane class need not
authorize the added cuts. This distinction remains an explicit limitation.

## 6. Projection-extreme source fibers in larger finite bases

The same zero-cost truncation argument applies to a projection-extreme source
fiber in any finite compatible polytopal family, whenever a normalized finite
local variational representation can be rederived in the ENLARGED family
including the cuts, with a realizable strictification and constraint
qualification for all coupled target conditions. The existence of a stress
before adjoining the cut parameters is insufficient. Such an index cannot be the
target of a nontrivial convex combination of other projection indices.
Shrinking it therefore improves every compatibility inequality in which it
appears as a source and creates no new incoming target condition.

For a constraint h_Kz(n)>=sum_w p_w h_Kw(n), a truncation of an extreme source
e with p_e>0 supplies a support bonus p_e sigma. Its sigma stationarity forces
the multiplier of that constraint to vanish if n exposes a nonfacet face in
Ke. For an interior source index, incoming target inequalities may worsen;
no such elimination is claimed without separately controlling those costs.
